questions.question: When backing a truck, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the driver's side mirror.
Use only the passenger's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check both side mirrors often when backing to see hazards behind your vehicle. Use a helper to watch blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: What should you check during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection of the engine, check the oil level, coolant level, and condition of hoses.

questions.question: If hazardous materials are leaking and the driver has no phone, what should they do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call for help.
Drive to a hazardous materials clean-up facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials leak, do not drive more than necessary. More area will become contaminated. Park your vehicle, secure it, stay with it, and contact emergency personnel. If you have no phone, send someone else for help.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brake drums or shoes?

options.text: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that are not covered in brake fluid
questions.explanation: Check brakes for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn thin. Brake fluid on shoes is a problem, not normal.

questions.question: What should you do before backing up?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk the path to check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk the path to check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out of the cab and check your path for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both mirrors.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: On the front, rear, and both sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and both sides.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of a vehicle with hazardous cargo. They must be readable from any direction.

questions.question: What should a safety belt do?
questions.explanation: The safety belt must be securely mounted, adjustable, latch properly, and not be ripped or frayed.

questions.question: What should a driver of a tank vehicle do?
questions.explanation: When driving a tank vehicle, increase your following distance. Liquid can surge forward when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What should you do if the brakes cannot build hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Hold the brake pedal down as far as it will go.

questions.explanation: If your brakes will not build pressure, try shifting to a lower gear, pumping the brakes, or using the emergency brake.

questions.question: What does a driver need to accept hazardous materials, if the package is safe?
questions.explanation: If a package is safe and follows regulations, you can accept the shipper's certification that it was packaged properly.

questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: It should only be used in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Blocking keeps cargo from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: When you must back up, backing toward the driver's side is:

options.text: Only recommended when it is raining.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side when you must back up. This gives you the best view of where you are going.

questions.question: Drivers stuck behind slow vehicles often:
questions.explanation: Many drivers follow slow vehicles too closely. If someone is tailgating you, let them pass.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials, what should you do?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver refuel.

questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. Someone must always hold the nozzle and control the fuel flow.

questions.question: Before driving a tank, you should not:

options.text: Assume pipes and hoses have no leaks.
Check the tank for dents or leaks.
Make sure all valves are in the correct positions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume pipes and hoses have no leaks.
questions.explanation: Before driving a tank, check it for leaks. Look at the tank, pipes, connections, and hoses. Make sure all valves are in the right positions before loading, unloading, or moving the vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe level?

options.text: Pull over and check the problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the problem.
questions.explanation: High coolant temperature can mean the engine may fail or catch fire. Stop safely as soon as you can and find out what is wrong.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to turn left safely. When two left turn lanes are available, start your turn in the right lane.

questions.question: What determines your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Your BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Only time can lower your BAC as your body processes the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: When are drivers usually least alert?
questions.explanation: Drivers are usually less alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: When transporting hazardous materials, where should placards be placed?

options.text: On all four sides of the vehicle.
Only for Class A licensed drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all four sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle when required.
